line: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 Aura Edition (2026, Panther Lake)
config_name: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 — Core Ultra 7 356H, 32GB LPDDR5, 1TB SSD, 14" 2.8K 120Hz matte OLED

specs.keyboard_notes: ThinkPad keyboard 1.5mm travel, TrackPoint, haptic touchpad

price.notes: +~CAD350 over 512GB tier; Lenovo CA configurator pricing.

reviews.quote: The reason to pick up the X1 Carbon Gen 14 is the increased repairability rather than anything resembling an increase in performance.
The X1 Carbon and the T14s are the superior options with the more advanced dual-fan cooling. They run very quietly as well, all things considered.

praises: Space Frame redesign means SSD, battery and ports are swappable — first X1 owners can keep the machine past warranty
Matte 2.8K 120Hz OLED is the best 14-inch panel on any business laptop; no visible flicker
Still ~1.0 kg — lightest in class by a wide margin
TrackPoint + haptic touchpad combo; ThinkPad keyboard remains best-in-class
Dual-fan cooling stays silent on Balanced for office/code workloads
complaints: Battery regression vs Gen 13 — several hours shorter in pro testing
No CPU performance uplift over Lunar Lake Gen 13
Lenovo's perpetual eCoupon pricing makes the real price hard to pin down
Bottom-firing speakers thin on conference calls

design_philosophy: Lenovo's flagship business ultraportable: carbon-fiber/magnesium chassis, classic ThinkPad DNA, maximum lightness with full portage. Gen 14's Space Frame prioritises repairability and cooling for corporate fleets kept 3-5 years.
rating_notes: Same reviewed config as 01 with 1TB instead of 512GB (CNET reviewed the OLED Gen 14); storage delta does not move ratings. Image from lenovo.com CA CDN.
